description: Pinkish-red walls of the outer ear canal lead to a translucent, yellowish-white eardrum. A small black arrow points at a yellowish-orange patch near the eardrum, which could be discharge or a sign of inflammation. The skin is smooth with only slight differences in texture, and there is no obvious redness, swelling, or fluid.

Yellow-brown, wax-like material fills part of the ear canal here, with the eardrum showing as a thin, round membrane behind it. The tissue around it is pinkish-red with a few slightly redder spots. Swelling, fluid, and crusting are not evident, and there is no sign of an air bubble, scarring, or blockage.

Cutting across the outer ear canal and eardrum, this view shows a thin, translucent eardrum with some yellowish-brown, wax-like material on its surface. The skin around it is reddish-pink with mild redness and some texture. Nothing points to swelling, fluid, crusting, blockage, or other irregularities.

The eardrum looks intact in this close shot of the ear canal, with a little yellowish-brown, wax-like material sitting on its surface. Reddish skin surrounds it, showing some texture and slight changes in tone. Swelling, fluid, and crusting are absent, and no other structures such as teeth, tongue, or throat appear in the frame.

This round cross-section of tissue is most likely the eardrum and the structures around it. The eardrum is thin and translucent with a yellowish-brown tint, and a few blood vessels and patches of reddish-pink tissue can be seen. It reflects light, which suggests how thin it is. Fluid, crusting, and blockage are not present, and the tissue is evenly reddish-pink with no clear signs of inflammation or swelling. Lighting is good and the detail is sharp.

Along its edge, the eardrum has a yellowish-brown tint and looks thin and translucent. The skin of the outer ear canal around it is reddish-pink, with fine lines and some texture. There is no obvious redness, swelling, fluid, or crusting.

Narrow and lined with yellowish-brown, wax-like material on its inner wall, this ear canal ends at a thin, translucent eardrum. The surrounding tissue is pinkish-red with some texture and uneven spots. No obvious swelling, fluid, or crusting is present.

Yellow, brown, and reddish patches make up a round area with a small dark circle near its center. The tissue looks soft and uneven, with yellowish-brown discoloration in places, and parts of the ear canal and eardrum can be made out. Blurriness, bright spots, and shadows make fine details hard to read. No obvious redness, swelling, fluid, or crusting.

Inside a round opening in the tissue sits an irregular yellowish mass. Reddish-pink skin surrounds it, with lighter patches near the edges. The ear canal runs along the left side and the eardrum is partly visible in the center. Wax, redness, and fluid are all absent, the surrounding tissue is smooth with some variation in color, and nothing else abnormal stands out.

Irregular yellowish-brown patches show up along a curved ear canal that looks a bit textured and has some debris in it. The eardrum appears as a thin, translucent membrane. Dark, somewhat shiny tissue surrounds it. No clear redness, swelling, fluid, or crusting.

At the center of the frame is a bright, irregular patch, with mostly dark tissue around it and some yellowish-brown areas near the edge. The eardrum shows as a thin, translucent line, and the nearby skin looks smooth with light brown or yellowish discoloration. No clear structures, redness, swelling, or fluid are visible.
